question: A man suffering from bronchial asthma is undergoing a chronic treatment lasting several years with glucocorticoids. Which of the following adverse reactions detected in said patient is not due to the prolonged use of corticoid therapy ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Glucocorticoid therapy -> poor healing of wounds -> 80% CHAIN: Glucocorticoid therapy -> osteoporosis -> 90% CHAIN: Glucocorticoid therapy -> arterial hypotension -> 10% CHAIN: Glucocorticoid therapy -> thinning of the skin -> 90% CHAIN: Glucocorticoid therapy -> muscular atrophy -> 80%
analysis: Arterial hypotension is not a common adverse reaction associated with prolonged use of corticosteroid therapy. The other options, poor healing of wounds, osteoporosis, thinning of the skin, and muscular atrophy, are well-documented side effects of chronic glucocorticoid treatment.
